item.title: Help with creating numbers on a log10 plot
item.description:
Hi there! I'm relatively new to coding and still finding my footing with it—it can definitely be a challenge. I work in scientific research, and from time to time I need to process and visualize data using RStudio.
Right now, I'm working on a poster presentation for next week, and I could use some help with creating a few graphs. For the first one, I’m trying to plot N₂O emissions against air temperature using a log10 scale on the y-axis. Here's the script I have so far:
# Create geom_smooth chart for N2O related to Tair ggplot(field_all_data, aes(x = T_air, y = N2O_mg_m2_h1)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) + theme_minimal() + scale_y_log10() + stat_cor(method = "pearson", label.x = 4, label.y = 3) + labs(x = expression("Air temperature" ~ (degree*C)), y = "N2O (mg/m²/h)", title = "N2O Emissions by Air Temperature")
My issue is that my N₂O values range from -0.76 to 711 mg/m²/h, and I know log10 can't handle negative or zero values. I also don't want to use continuous scale as the majority of my values are clustered below 10. What's the best way to handle this kind of data so I can still use a log scale for the y-axis?
